key_insight: A calibration-aware graph RL router can outperform gate-count-driven quantum circuit routing by avoiding poorly calibrated couplers, improving exact fidelity on noisy hardware.
engineering_relevance: This suggests compiler routing policies should incorporate live device calibration data, not just swap-count or depth, when targeting near-term quantum processors.
method: Train a graph-based routing policy with proximal policy optimization (PPO).
Use same-day IBM Heron r2 calibration data to select hardware-edge SWAPs.
Compare routed circuits against SABRE-best20 and target-aware SABRE using exact simulated fidelity.
evidence_signal: Across nine MQT Bench circuits and three calibration snapshots, pooled mean exact fidelity was 0.727 for the learned router versus 0.440 for SABRE-best20 and 0.481 for target-aware SABRE.
watch_item: The fidelity gains come with higher two-qubit gate counts and are not uniform: under the fixed tree action graph, all 10q circuit families favored SABRE-best20.
paper_title: Graph Reinforcement Learning for Calibration-Aware Quantum Circuit Routing
